1.

    A smoke detector uses the radioactive nuclide americium-241. These greyed out bits
      aren’t too important.

     The americium is contained in a chamber that is open to the air. There are two
     electrodes in the chamber that are connected to a power supply and a current
     sensor.





     Americium-241 emits alpha particles that ionize the air in the chamber. Each
      ionization forms one positive ion and one electron; these are called an ion pair. The
     electrons and the positive ions move towards the electrodes and the sensor detects
    a current in the air.

    When smoke enters the chamber, fewer ion pairs are formed and the current in the
     sensor decreases, sounding an alarm.

     The decay constant of americium-241 is 5.08 × 10−11 s−1.
     The chamber is 0.10 m in each dimension.

(a)

    Deduce whether the radioactive source will need to be replaced during the life of
          the detector.
